question_text: What is the capital of your state?

why_it_matters.text: A state's capital is where state laws are made and state government runs. Saint Paul has been Minnesota's capital since 1849 — even before Minnesota became a state in 1858. Knowing your state capital connects you to the place where decisions about Minnesota's schools, roads, taxes, and laws actually get made.

fun_fact.text: The Minnesota State Capitol in Saint Paul was designed by Cass Gilbert, a young architect from St. Paul. He finished it in 1905. He did such a good job that 30 years later, he was hired to design an even bigger building: the U.S. Supreme Court building in Washington, D.C. Same architect, both buildings, marble and dome and all.
